title: Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia: FIGO/WHO Prognostic Scoring & Choriocarcinoma: Diagnosis, Risk Stratification and EMA-CO
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: Berek & Hacker's Gynecologic Oncology 7th Edition Ch 22
FIGO Cancer Report 2021: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Gestational Trophoblastic Neoplasia (Version 1.2024)

steps.say: The diagnosis of post-molar gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is established through strict biochemical criteria based on serial serum human chorionic gonadotropin measurements.
steps.tx: The **FIGO diagnostic criteria for GTN** establish malignancy following molar evacuation if: hCG levels demonstrate a **plateau across 4 values in 3 weeks** (Days 1, 7, 14, 21), a consecutive **rise across 3 values in 2 weeks** (Days 1, 7, 14), **histologic choriocarcinoma**, or **persistence >=6 months**.

steps.say: Once a diagnosis of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is established, every patient must be categorized using the modified FIGO WHO prognostic scoring system.
steps.tx: The **FIGO/WHO prognostic score** categorizes GTN into **low-risk 0-6** and **high-risk >=7** disease. The scoring algorithm sums points across **8 prognostic factors**: age, antecedent pregnancy, interval from index pregnancy, pre-treatment hCG, largest tumor size, site of metastases, number of metastases, and prior failed chemotherapy.

steps.say: Certain metastatic anatomical sites and antecedent pregnancy types carry disproportionate prognostic weight in the modified scoring system.
steps.tx: In the WHO scoring matrix, **brain/liver metastases 4 points** reflects profound risk of hemorrhagic fatality, whereas **lung metastases 0 points** carries minimal adverse weight. Similarly, disease following a **term pregnancy 2 points** reflects worse biology than following a **molar pregnancy 0 points**.

left.title: Low Scoring Variables (0-1 Points)
points: Lung metastases or absent metastases (0 points)

right.title: High Scoring Variables (2-4 Points)
points: Brain or liver metastases (4 points each)
Prior failed single-agent or multi-agent chemotherapy (2-4 points)

steps.say: Patients stratified with low-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia are treated definitively with single-agent cytotoxic chemotherapy regimens.
steps.tx: For **low-risk GTN chemotherapy** (score 0 to 6), primary treatment comprises single-agent methotrexate or **actinomycin D**. The standard **methotrexate-leucovorin 8-day regimen** (methotrexate 1 mg/kg on Days 1, 3, 5, 7 with leucovorin rescue on Days 2, 4, 6, 8) achieves a primary **cure rate ~100%**.

steps.say: High-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia requires immediate aggressive multi-agent combination systemic chemotherapy.
steps.tx: Patients with **high-risk GTN EMA-CO** (score >=7) receive combination chemotherapy alternating weekly: Day 1 **Etoposide Methotrexate Actinomycin D** with folinic acid, followed on Day 8 by **Cyclophosphamide Vincristine**, achieving a long-term **cure rate 85-90%** even in widely metastatic presentations. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

nodes.label: Week 1 (Days 1-2): Administer Etoposide, Methotrexate (with FA rescue), and Actinomycin D
Monitor serial weekly serum beta-hCG until negative (<5 mIU/mL)
Attain overall long-term complete survival in 85% to 90% of high-risk patients

steps.say: Following normalization of serum hCG concentrations, consolidation chemotherapy cycles are essential to eradicate occult microscopic trophoblastic cells.
steps.tx: To eradicate microscopic residual disease and prevent relapse, **consolidation chemotherapy** must continue after hCG reaches normal: **2-3 cycles low-risk** disease and **3-4 cycles high-risk** disease, which provides effective **prevention of relapse** across all international trophoblastic disease registries. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

left.title: Low-Risk Consolidation Protocol
points: Administer 2 to 3 consolidation cycles after first normal hCG

right.title: High-Risk Consolidation Protocol
points: Continue multi-agent EMA-CO without dose reduction
Administer 3 to 4 consolidation cycles after first normal hCG
Essential to sterilize chemoresistant sanctuary sites in brain and liver

steps.say: Gestational choriocarcinoma is the most malignant form of gestational trophoblastic disease, displaying a characteristic histological architecture.
steps.tx: Gestational **choriocarcinoma** is a highly anaplastic, dimorphic malignancy displaying **biphasic syncytio- and cytotrophoblast** proliferation with complete **absence of chorionic villi**. Microscopically, it is characterized by sheets of atypical trophoblastic cells, **extensive hemorrhage and necrosis**, and early haematogenous dissemination. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

left.title: Hydatidiform Mole Histology
points: Presence of hydropic, edematous chorionic villi
Cistern formation within swollen villous stroma

right.title: Choriocarcinoma Histology
points: Complete absence of chorionic villous architecture
Biphasic sheets of syncytiotrophoblast and cytotrophoblast
Massive hemorrhage and extensive central coagulation necrosis

steps.say: The presence of central nervous system metastases in patients with choriocarcinoma requires multimodal therapy to prevent fatal intracranial hemorrhage.
steps.tx: In patients with **brain metastases in GTN**, multimodal therapy combines **whole brain RT 30 Gy** (delivered in 10 fractions) or **intrathecal methotrexate** (12.5 mg) with modified EMA-CO utilizing **high-dose MTX 1 g/m2** to achieve therapeutic central nervous system drug concentrations.
